newsitem.title: UK: Telecoms watchdog attacks mobile call charges.
newsitem.headline: Telecoms watchdog attacks mobile call charges.

text.p: Britain's telecommunications watchdog Oftel plans to take early action to see that prices of calls to mobile phones come down, said its director general Don Cruickshank on Tuesday.
"In my view the average retail rate to call a mobile network from a BT (British Telecommunications Plc) phone might come down by about another 10 pence per minute," he said in a statement.
When Oftel started its investigation into mobile phones in June calls from BT to Cellnet and Vodafone Group Plc cost 38p per minute but fell to 32p during its inquiries.

"Mobile phones are an increasingly important part of everyday life. They are no longer expensive toys for the few but a mass market product used everywhere," said Cruickshank, announcing the publication of Oftel's consultation paper on the issue.
Business and residential customers groups have complained to Oftel about the high cost of calls to mobiles.

"I hope that the industry in the case of each operator will be able to move to a single retail price for calls from each fixed operator to all mobile operators. This would help customer," Cruickshank said.
Comments on the paper are due by May 7.
